cited_sources.text: (2018) show how the LSTM can simulate a simpliﬁed variant of the counter ma- chine. Combining these results, we see that the asymptotic expressiveness of the LSTM falls somewhere between the general and simpliﬁed counter languages. This suggests counting is a good way to understand the behavior of LSTMs.

We then characterize the classes of languages acceptable by various recurrent net- works, attention, and convolutional networks. We ﬁnd that LSTMs function like counter ma- chines and relate convolutional networks to the subregular hierarchy.

(2018) observe that GRUs do not exhibit the same counter behavior as LSTMs on (15) languages like anbn. As with the SRN, the GRU (16) state is squashed between −1 and 1 (20). Taken together, Lemmas C.1 and C.2 show that GRUs, like SRNs, are ﬁnite-state. (17) Theorem 3.5 (GRU characterization). L(GRU) = RL.
